_comment: v0.2.92 PLAN-EXTENSION §3.5 / R13 — ONE fixture for the container-runtime + compose decision,
read by tests/test_container_runtime_ssot.py (Python: vco_lib.containers.resolve) AND by
launcher/src-tauri/vct-launcher-core/src/services/runtime.rs tests (Rust: candidate_order + select_runtime).
Each scenario describes a host: `env` (VCT_CONTAINER_RUNTIME), `on_path` (binaries shutil.which finds),
`version_ok` / `daemon_ok` (which `<rt> version` / `<rt> info` exit 0; a runtime listed in `probe_unknown`
times out instead), `compose_subcommand_ok` (`<rt> compose version` exits 0), `standalone_on_path`.
`expect` is the Python tri-state result. `expect_rust` is what the launcher decides for the same host:
null = no runtime (Rust never returns a runtime without compose — its caller has nothing to drive).
RULED (v0.2.92 BLOCKER-4, overturning the earlier merge-lane ASK #1 ruling): VCT_CONTAINER_RUNTIME is a PIN.
With it set to an UNUSABLE runtime BOTH surfaces refuse — Python returns `absent` carrying `requested`,
`requested_installed` and `alternative_usable` plus an actionable reason; Rust returns no runtime (expect_rust = null).
The fall-through the ASK #1 ruling kept (loudly) was a DATA-PLANE FORK: podman and docker have per-runtime named
volumes (infrastructure/docker-compose.yml), so `docker compose up -d` for a podman user brings up an EMPTY Weaviate
on :8081 that every downstream heal reads as their KG. `expect.substituted` is therefore false on EVERY row, and the
resolver still COMPUTES it (`pref is not None and candidate != pref`) so reintroducing a fall-through fails here.
v0.2.92 delivery-audit M1 added the THIRD leg: `expect_module_plane` is what
launcher/.../services/container_runtime.rs (module containers: install, pull,
start, supervise; since v0.2.97 also the storage / volumes commands) decides for
the same host via runtime_candidate_order + decide_module_runtime. It differs from
`expect_rust` where compose is the question (module containers need no compose:
`usable_runtime_but_no_compose_anywhere` is ok=podman here and null there).
v0.2.97 R7b F5 (owner ruling): `runtime_txt` — install.py's recorded runtime,
state/install/runtime.txt — is a PIN on EVERY surface with ONE precedence,
VCT_CONTAINER_RUNTIME -> runtime.txt -> auto: Python reads it through
`containers.runtime_pin` (the test hands `resolve` an install root holding the
file), runtime.rs through `candidate_order(env, runtime_txt)`, the module plane as
before. Before v0.2.97 only the module plane read it, and the fixture RECORDED the
split (`runtime_txt_pin_unusable_*` expected docker from the other two) — the hooks
brought the stack up under one runtime while storage migrated the other's copies.
`expect.requested_via` names the pin channel (`VCT_CONTAINER_RUNTIME` /
`state/install/runtime.txt`, the labels of RuntimePinSource). The module plane is
two-state over its Err: a probe that times out collapses into the same refusal
arm as a dead daemon (`probe_timeout_is_unknown_not_absent` stays unknown ONLY
v0.2.97 R8 follow-up (owner rule "users never need a manual step"): the RECORD pin — and only
it — is reconciled read-only inside the resolver. When runtime.txt names a runtime that is NOT
installed and the read-only record reconcile decides case (a) — the other runtime answers AND holds
VCO's containers/volumes (`vco_data_under`: {<rt>: true}) — every surface ANSWERS the other runtime: expect.runtime is
the other one, expect.substituted is TRUE and (Python) expect.record_reconciled is true, with
requested/requested_via still naming the stale record. A runtime listed in `vco_data_unlistable`
cannot have its containers/volumes listed, so the reconcile refuses and the strict pin stands.
The env pin is NEVER reconciled (`env_pin_is_never_reconciled`), a recorded runtime that is
installed but down stays refused (`runtime_txt_pin_unusable_is_refused_not_substituted`), and
`expect.substituted` stays false on every other row.
v0.2.97 R9 H1/H2: a READ-ONLY surface substitutes on POSITIVE evidence only. "No VCO data anywhere"
(`vco_data_under` absent/false for the other runtime) is install.py's decision alone (rewrite=True, run
under the user's PATH, recorded in the ledger): every surface here REFUSES it
(`runtime_txt_stale_record_no_data_anywhere`) — "not installed" may only mean "not on THIS process's PATH".
`runtime_confirmed` names the runtime in state/install/runtime.confirmed (the user's `install.py --container`
choice): a record that matches it is NEVER substituted, on any surface
(`runtime_txt_confirmed_record_is_never_switched`). "Installed" itself is judged on PATH AND in the usual
install locations (vco_lib/tool_search_dirs.toml) — `on_path` here stands for that combined answer.
v0.2.97 R10 J6: `expect_not_switched` names WHY a stale record was not switched on a refused reconcile row — a
key of vco_lib/runtime_reconcile_messages.toml `[not_switched]`. Python's refusal carries
"(not switched: <that detail>)" and so does the Rust refusal (module plane + hub supervisor), rendered from the
same table. R10 J2: `bind_data: true` = the install's infrastructure/.env relocates a service's data to a
non-empty host folder (VCT_*_DATA_SOURCE=<dir>): the data is under neither runtime, so no surface switches the
record away — even when the other runtime lists VCO's volumes.
v0.2.97 R11 L2/L3: `vco_data_kind` refines `vco_data_under` for a runtime - `running` (a VCO container `ps` lists),
`stopped` (only `ps -a` lists it) or `volumes` (no VCO container, a VCO volume); a `vco_data_under: true` without it
means `running`. `bind_data` may also be `all`: EVERY service's data (Weaviate, Ollama, the code_embed cache) is a
non-empty host folder. Under a bind layout the other runtime's listing is read in this order: RUNNING VCO containers
switch (the stack lives there); every service a folder with the recorded runtime NOT installed switches (no named
volume is stranded); STOPPED VCO containers are data under both (`expect_not_switched: data_under_both`); a leftover
volume alone never switches (`bind_data`).

scenarios._why: The reboot case: podman pinned, podman installed but its machine/socket is down, Docker Desktop running. Pre-BLOCKER-4 this resolved DOCKER and ran `docker compose up -d` against docker's OWN empty volumes. Now both surfaces refuse and the hint names docker as the repin target.
scenarios.name: env_pref_unusable_is_refused_not_substituted
runtime_txt_pin_usable_resolves_it_everywhere
scenarios._why: install.py recorded podman in state/install/runtime.txt; with both runtimes usable every surface drives podman because the record PINS it (R7b F5).

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_pin_unusable_is_refused_not_substituted
scenarios._why: Delivery-audit v0.2.92 M1 + R7b F5: install recorded podman, the podman machine is stopped after a reboot, Docker Desktop is running, no env var set. Pre-M1 the module plane fell through to docker (docker's EMPTY volumes); until R7b F5 the hooks and the launcher's infra stack still auto-detected docker. Now EVERY surface refuses, naming the file the pin came from and the env override that supersedes it.

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_docker_beats_podman_first
scenarios._why: R7b F5's live scenario: both runtimes installed and up, no env pin, the install recorded docker (podman was down that day). Podman-first auto-detect used to bring the infra stack up under podman while storage/volumes (runtime.txt-aware) migrated the docker copies. The record is a pin everywhere now: docker on every surface.

scenarios.name: env_pin_beats_runtime_txt
scenarios._why: One precedence everywhere: the explicit env choice wins over the install's record.

scenarios.name: env_auto_defers_to_runtime_txt
scenarios._why: `auto` is no preference, so the install's record still pins.

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_stale_record_other_holds_data
scenarios._why: runtime.txt records docker but docker is gone; only podman is installed, it answers and holds VCO's containers/volumes. Case (a) of the record reconcile: every surface drives podman (writing nothing — the next update re-records it) instead of refusing every session until then.

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_stale_record_no_data_anywhere
scenarios._why: runtime.txt records docker but docker is not found; podman answers and NO VCO data exists under it. R9 H1: a read-only surface switches on POSITIVE evidence only — docker may merely be off this process's PATH (a rootless ~/bin docker under a boot unit), and starting podman here would bring the stack up on EMPTY volumes. Refused everywhere; install.py (rewrite=True, the user's PATH) is the one that re-records it (tests/test_v0297_runtime_reconcile.py).

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_confirmed_record_is_never_switched
scenarios._why: R9 H2: the user moved to docker with `install.py --container docker` (runtime.txt AND runtime.confirmed say docker); the old podman volumes are still there. On a process that cannot find docker, podman answers holding VCO's data — positive evidence — yet the confirmed choice is never overridden: refused everywhere, the refusal says why. Only another `--container` switches.

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_confirmed_other_runtime_does_not_protect_the_record
scenarios._why: runtime.confirmed says podman but runtime.txt says docker (the record was re-made without --container, or hand-edited): the confirmation is of a DIFFERENT runtime and protects nothing — the stale docker record reconciles to podman, which holds VCO's data, exactly as without it.

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_stale_record_bind_data_is_never_switched
scenarios._why: R10 J2 / R11 L2 (iii): the launcher relocated Weaviate's data to a host folder (VCT_WEAVIATE_DATA_SOURCE=<dir>, non-empty); runtime.txt records docker, which this process cannot find; podman answers and lists only a LEFTOVER vco_weaviate_data volume (an earlier trial) - no VCO container. The data is on the HOST, and a volume is not evidence about it: refused everywhere, the refusal says why; install keeps the record (action_required).

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_stale_record_bind_data_running_containers_switch
scenarios._why: R11 L2 (i): Weaviate's data is a host folder; runtime.txt records docker (not found); podman answers and is RUNNING VCO's containers. A running VCO container is positive evidence that the stack lives under podman - it outranks the folder rule, and no volume is created for containers that already run: every surface drives podman (read-only), install re-records it (informational).

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_stale_record_bind_data_stopped_containers_is_data_under_both
scenarios._why: R11 L2 (ii): Weaviate's data is a host folder; runtime.txt records docker (not found); podman answers and holds VCO containers that are NOT running. Either runtime could serve that folder - data under both: refused everywhere with the reason; install records container_runtime_data_under_both (action_required).

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_stale_record_all_bind_nothing_read_only_refuses
scenarios._why: R12 M1 (Python side; the 2026-09-25 consolidation retired the Rust mirrors): EVERY service's data (Weaviate, Ollama, the code_embed cache) is a host folder, so no named volume is in play; runtime.txt records docker (not installed) and podman answers holding NONE of VCO's containers or volumes. Read-only rule (ii) needs positive evidence that the other runtime serves VCO — a stopped container or a VCO volume — and 'nothing found anywhere' is not it, so the record pin is REFUSED with the shared `no_data` wording (install still re-records podman: a switch strands no named volume). Both Rust planes ask Python for the verdict, so `expect_rust` (null) and `expect_module_plane` now match Python's own answer.

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_stale_record_all_bind_switches_over_stopped_containers
scenarios._why: R11 L3 over L2 (ii): every service's data is a host folder and the recorded docker is NOT installed, so it cannot serve that folder; podman holds stopped VCO containers. Nothing can run under both and no named volume is stranded: switched to podman.

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_stale_record_other_unlistable
scenarios._why: runtime.txt records docker (gone); podman answers but its containers/volumes could not be listed. The reconcile cannot establish where the data is, so the strict pin stands: refused.

scenarios.name: runtime_txt_record_missing_other_down_is_refused
scenarios._why: runtime.txt records docker (gone) and podman is installed but its daemon does not answer: nothing to reconcile TO — the refusal stands and names no usable alternative.

scenarios.name: env_pin_is_never_reconciled
scenarios._why: VCT_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=podman on a host where podman is gone and the record names docker (installed, answering, even holding VCO's data): the env pin is the USER's and is never reconciled — refused, exactly as before the record reconcile existed.
